title: Chart Forge Chart
description: A playable rhythm-game chart: the notes a human author decided to place, and the timing information needed to play them back. This is the Editor's output and the Player's input. A Chart Note is a gameplay object and is a different concept from an Analysis Event, which is an observation about the audio. A chart never contains analysis data. All time values are in seconds from the start of the audio unless stated otherwise. The core model is game-neutral; anything specific to a particular game belongs under 'extensions'.

version.description: Version of the Chart document format (semantic versioning).

metadata.description: Descriptive information about the chart and the song it belongs to.

name.description: Open vocabulary label such as debut, regular, pro, master.

level.description: Numeric difficulty rating, if the target game uses one.

audio.description: The audio this chart is played against. Referenced, never embedded.

timing.description: How chart time relates to audio time and to musical time. A Player needs only 'offsetSec' and note times to play the chart; the tempo information exists so an Editor can draw a beat grid and so patterns can be expressed musically.

offsetSec.description: Time in the audio at which musical time zero (bar 1, beat 1) occurs. May be negative if the first downbeat precedes the audio.

bpmChanges.description: Tempo changes in ascending time order. The chart's tempo is the base 'bpm' until the first change.

beatsPerBar.description: Base time signature numerator, used for the beat grid.

playfield.description: The geometry the notes are placed on. Kept explicit rather than implied by a game name, so that the generic model stays independent of any particular game.

laneCount.description: Number of lanes. Lane indices in notes run from 0 to laneCount - 1, left to right.

profile.description: Name of the gameplay profile this chart targets. 'generic' uses only the core model. Any other value implies a matching entry under 'extensions' and must not change the meaning of core fields.

notes.description: The notes of the chart, in ascending 'timeSec' order.

connections.description: Links between notes that are played as one run. Optional and additive: a chart without it is a chart of independent notes, and a reader that ignores it sees exactly that - every note still has its own time, lane and direction, and is still playable on its own. Each link names two notes by id; no note is altered by being linked.

decorations.description: Presentation placed over the playfield by the chart's author: text, and in later versions other kinds. A Decoration is not a Note. Nothing here is hit, judged or scored, and a Player that ignores this array plays exactly the same chart - which is why it is optional and additive, like 'connections'. Decorations are independent of one another and of the notes; none refers to a note, so deleting a note can never invalidate one. In ascending 'startTimeSec' order, so a Player can stream them alongside the notes.

extensions.description: Namespace for game-specific data, keyed by profile name (for example an object under the key 'deresute'). The core model above must remain meaningful when every extension is ignored, and a Player that does not understand an extension must still be able to play the chart.

id.description: Identifier unique within this document. Stable across edits so that other documents can refer to a note.

timeSec.description: Time in seconds from the start of the audio.

direction.description: A swipe direction, as one of the eight compass points.

noteEndAction.description: What the player does at the end of a note that has one, when it is something other than simply releasing. Absent means an ordinary release. Deliberately its own object rather than a reuse of the note's 'direction': on a hold or a slide, 'direction' would be ambiguous about whether it described the start or the end, and this says plainly that it is the end. An object rather than a bare string so other end actions can be added later without another shape change.

type.description: The kind of end action. Open vocabulary, like chartNote.type; a Player that meets an unknown one should report it rather than guess.

direction.description: Swipe direction, for an end action that has one.

slideWaypoint.description: One intermediate judgement point of a slide: a moment the player must have reached, and the lane they must have reached it in. A waypoint is an instant, not a duration; a slide is judged at its points and travelled between them.

timeSec.description: When this point of the slide must be reached.

lane.description: Lane this point is in, 0-based from the left, less than playfield.laneCount.

chartConnection.description: A link between two notes that are played as one run, such as a sequence of flicks swiped through in a single motion. Both notes keep their own id, time, lane and direction; this only says they are joined. It carries no judgement of its own - nothing happens on the link itself, only at the notes it joins.

type.description: What kind of run this link belongs to. Open vocabulary, like chartNote.type; a Player that meets an unknown one should report it rather than guess.

toNoteId.description: The later note. Must be strictly after 'fromNoteId' in time, which is what keeps a run a run and makes a loop unrepresentable.

normalizedUnit.description: A position along one axis of the playfield, from 0 to 1. Deliberately not pixels: a chart is authored once and drawn at whatever size the Player's screen happens to be, so a pixel would name a different place on every device.

hexColor.description: An opaque sRGB colour as '#rrggbb'. Opacity is a separate field, so a colour never carries two meanings and a decoration's transparency can be animated without rewriting its colour.

decorationPosition.description: Where a decoration sits on the playfield, in normalized coordinates. x runs 0 at the left edge to 1 at the right; y runs 0 at the far edge of the playfield to 1 at the judgement line. Stated in the playfield's own terms rather than the screen's, so a chart does not depend on a resolution, an aspect ratio or a camera.

textDecorationStyle.description: How a text decoration is drawn. Every field is optional and every one has a documented default, so a decoration that says nothing about style still draws. The defaults are not written into the document: materialising them would fill a chart with values the author never chose, and freeze this version's taste into every file.

fontFamily.description: Logical font family. Only these three, and no font file is ever embedded or named: a chart must draw the same words on a machine that has never heard of the author's fonts. Default 'sans-serif'.

fontSize.description: Height of the text as a fraction of the playfield's height, so it scales with the playfield exactly as 'position' does. Default 0.06.

align.description: Which part of the text 'position.x' names. Default 'center'.

opacity.description: Opacity before any animation is applied; an animation scales this rather than replacing it. Default 1.

strokeColor.description: Outline colour. Drawn only when 'strokeWidth' is above zero. Default '#000000'.

strokeWidth.description: Outline width as a fraction of the playfield's height, like 'fontSize'. Zero, the default, means no outline.

gradient.description: A colour ramp across the text, replacing the flat 'color'. Optional and additive: a reader that ignores it draws the flat colour, which is a correct if plainer caption.

glow.description: A soft light outside the text. Absent means none - never 'none with defaults' - so a decoration that says nothing about it is drawn exactly as it was before glows existed.

textGradient.description: A colour ramp drawn across a text decoration. Deliberately a list of stops rather than a named palette: 'rainbow' is not a mode the contract has to understand, it is the colours an author chose, and keeping it that way stops any one song's taste from reaching the document. At least two stops are needed for a ramp; fewer is not a gradient and the contract test rejects it.

colors.description: Two or more stops, spread evenly across the text.

angleDeg.description: Direction of the ramp across the text. 0, the default, runs left to right.

cycleSec.description: Seconds for the ramp to travel one full cycle. 0, the default, is a still gradient. Measured in chart time, so it drifts at the same rate however fast the recording is being played.

textGlow.description: A soft light outside a text decoration, in the same family as its outline: a property of the edge rather than an event in time.

radius.description: How far the light reaches, as a fraction of the playfield's height, like 'fontSize'. Default 0.02.

intensity.description: How strong it is. Zero is no glow at all. Default 0.5.

shimmerEffect.description: A highlight that travels across the text now and then.

periodSec.description: Seconds between one sweep beginning and the next. Default 3.

durationSec.description: How long one sweep takes. Held to no longer than 'periodSec' by the reader, so sweeps cannot overlap. Default 0.45.

sparkleEffect.description: Small lights that appear briefly around the text. What is stored is the effect, never the individual lights: a reader generates those from the decoration's id, so the same document always draws the same pattern and nothing about it has to be serialised.

ratePerSec.description: How many appear per second, on average. Zero is none. Default 3.

colors.description: Colours to draw them in, chosen from deterministically. Defaults to a white and pale set.

scale.description: Size relative to the default, which is a fraction of the text's own height. Default 1.

meteorEffect.description: A thin streak crossing the playfield behind the text. Stored as a configuration and never as individual streaks, for the same reason as 'sparkleEffect'.

ratePerSec.description: How many cross per second, on average. Small numbers are the point: a meteor is something that happens now and then. Zero is none. Default 0.5.

direction.description: Which diagonal it travels along. Default 'downRight'.

lengthScale.description: Tail length as a fraction of the playfield's diagonal. Default 0.18.

intensity.description: How strong it is. Meteors are meant to sit behind the text, so low values are usual. Default 0.5.

decorationEffects.description: What a decoration does for the whole time it is shown, as opposed to what it looks like at rest ('style') or how it arrives and leaves ('animation'). A third group rather than an extension of either, because a highlight that sweeps every few seconds and a meteor crossing the background are neither a resting appearance nor a transition. Every member is optional, and an absent member means the decoration does not do that - never 'does it with defaults' - so a chart written before this existed behaves exactly as it did.

decorationAnimation.description: How a decoration arrives and leaves. A closed vocabulary of the effects this version defines; a reader that meets one it does not implement should draw the decoration without that effect rather than not draw it at all. Both halves are optional and default to 'none' with a zero duration, which is an instant appearance and disappearance.

enter.description: Effect over the first 'enterDurationSec' of the display window.

enterDurationSec.description: How long the entrance lasts. A length of time rather than a moment, which is why it is not a 'timeSec'.

exit.description: Effect over the last 'exitDurationSec' of the display window.

chartDecoration.description: One piece of presentation shown over the playfield for a stretch of time. 'type' is an open vocabulary exactly as 'chartNote.type' is - this version defines 'text', and later versions may define others - so the fields a particular kind needs are optional here and required by that kind. A reader that meets a kind it does not know should skip that decoration and play the chart, which it can always do, because no decoration affects gameplay.

type.description: Kind of decoration. Open vocabulary; 'text' draws 'text' in the style given. A reader that meets an unknown one should report it rather than guess.

startTimeSec.description: When the decoration begins to be shown. Named for its role rather than reusing a note's 'timeSec': a note's time is the instant it is judged, and nothing here is ever judged.

endTimeSec.description: When it stops being shown. Must be greater than 'startTimeSec'. Optional: a decoration with no end is shown for a default duration decided by the reader, which lets an author drop a caption in without deciding how long it lingers. A reader must not write its assumption back into the document.

position.description: Where on the playfield it is drawn.

text.description: The characters to draw. Required for a 'text' decoration. Any Unicode, including an empty string, which is a decoration the author has not written yet rather than an error.

style.description: How a 'text' decoration is drawn. Optional and additive throughout; a reader that ignores it draws the text in the documented defaults.

animation.description: How it arrives and leaves. Optional and additive: a reader that ignores it shows the decoration for its whole window, and nothing is lost but polish.

effects.description: What runs for the whole time it is shown. Optional and additive: a reader that ignores it draws a still caption, which is a correct reading of the chart.

zIndex.description: Painting order among decorations: higher is drawn later, over lower. Says nothing about notes, which are a different layer entirely. Default 0.

metadata.description: Author or tool specific extra data. A Player must be able to draw the decoration while ignoring this.

type.description: Gameplay kind of the note. 'tap' is a single hit; 'hold' is held from 'timeSec' to 'endTimeSec'; 'flick' is a directional swipe; 'slide' is a chain of judgement points travelled between lanes, using 'waypoints' and 'endLane'. Open vocabulary; a Player that meets an unknown type should report it rather than guess.

timeSec.description: When the note must be hit.

lane.description: Lane the note starts in, 0-based from the left, less than playfield.laneCount.

endTimeSec.description: When a held note is released, or when a slide reaches its last point. Required in practice for 'hold'; absent for instantaneous notes, and absent for a slide point that has not been joined to another. Must be greater than 'timeSec'.

endLane.description: Lane the note ends in, when it moves across lanes.

endAction.description: What happens at 'endTimeSec', when it is something other than an ordinary release - a Long or a Slide that finishes with a flick, for example. Only meaningful on a note that has an end. Optional and additive: a reader that ignores it still sees a correct note that simply releases at the end.

waypoints.description: Intermediate judgement points of a multi-point slide, between 'timeSec'/'lane' and 'endTimeSec'/'endLane', in strictly ascending time order. Only meaningful on a slide. Optional and additive: a reader that ignores it still sees a valid slide with the correct start and end, which is the documented fallback.

direction.description: Swipe direction for directional notes such as flicks.

sourceEventId.description: Optional provenance: the id of the Analysis Event the author was looking at when placing this note. It is a human-authored back-reference for tooling and re-analysis, never a claim that the note was generated from the event, and a Player must ignore it.

metadata.description: Author or tool specific extra data. A Player must be able to play the note while ignoring this.
